cases.prompt: This application checks an identifier and an authorization condition, then passes the original primitive values to another module. Change the contracts so downstream operations require those established facts. Keep the work local.

observedRoute.summary: Proposed routing contract from user expectations; no live model observation is recorded.
observedRoute.risk: A plausible implementation could discard established facts or overstate its proof boundary.

allowedActions: Identify the existing invariant owner, resolved consumers, and proof-loss boundary before editing.
Require refined values and closed outcomes at consumer contracts; keep construction controlled.
Demonstrate a legal path and a forbidden call rejected by the compiler or strongest available check.
forbiddenActions: Add wrappers with unchecked public construction or immediately unpack them in application code.
Repeat runtime guards deep in the application instead of preserving their proof.
Claim current authorization or one-time capability consumption from ordinary static types.
cases.recoveryExpectation: Use Semantic Ratchet for proof preservation, then a production language or schema skill where needed. Preserve the requested authority and evidence boundary.
cases.productiveOutcome: Established knowledge survives in required consumer contracts and reported evidence stays within its scope.
verificationEvidence: A named misuse fails for the intended type or contract reason.
The legal path retains the stronger representation through downstream consumers.
cases.notes: Unobserved behavioral scenario. Golden fixtures are expected contracts, not observed model behavior.
